# AI-use ledger

*Generated by `code/analysis/build_ai_use_ledger.py` from the reviewer and researcher labels in the CSV databases; do not edit by hand. The data are in `AI_USE_LEDGER.csv`. The narrative statement is `../AI_USE_STATEMENT.md`; the per-study view is `STUDY_AUDIT_TRAIL.csv`.*

This ledger says, stage by stage, which AI tool or model did what, how many records or rows carry its label, over which dates, and how many a human checked. It is meant to let a reader judge how much of the review rests on an AI's unverified judgment, and to let a critic target the weakest stage.

## What is NOT archived (read this before trying to reproduce or critique the AI work)

1. The conversation prompts for the main work. Title/abstract screening, full-text screening, extraction and risk-of-bias appraisal were done by Claude in interactive sessions with the researcher. What survives is the instructions it was given in files (above), the decisions with a written reason per record, and the scripts that wrote them (`code/provenance/`, from record batch 64 onward). The earliest scripts existed only in an ephemeral session scratchpad and are not recoverable (audit finding 11).
2. The exact model version behind most decisions. Labels record the tool and a date (`Claude-AI-fulltext-2026-09-16`), not a model identifier, so the model that produced a given row can only be bracketed by date. Only 60 early full-text rows carry a model name (`claude_sonnet_5`). The Codex (`gpt-5.6-sol`) and Gemini (`gemini-3.1-flash-lite`) passes record the model in the label.
3. Sampling settings and seeds. No temperature, seed or reasoning-effort setting is recorded for the Claude work. AI decisions are not deterministic: re-running the same prompt would not be expected to reproduce the same 26,222 title/abstract decisions or the same extractions.
4. An independent re-run. No second AI model repeated the whole first pass, and no human extracted any study. The second-model pass covers a sample of full-text decisions only.
5. A validated accuracy figure for the AI's extraction or risk-of-bias rating. The only measured error rates are for screening (the A16 audit of excludes) and, informally, the 2026-09-28 audit. A blind 60-study second-extraction sample is prepared and has not been done.

## How to use this to find the weak points

- The largest AI-only stages are the title/abstract exclusions, the full-text exclusions that were not adjudicated, every extraction, and every risk-of-bias rating. Pick a stage and test it: `AUDITING_GUIDE.md` §5 lists ways to challenge each.
- To re-screen or re-extract a sample, `../03_extraction/second_extractor/README.md` and `../02_screening/full_text/REVIEWER_2_PRIORITY_QUEUE_README.md` are ready-made.
- For one study, filter `STUDY_AUDIT_TRAIL.csv` on its `study_id`.
